learning_outcomes.text: Acquisition of basic notions related to the structure, properties, investigation methods, and processing of engineering materials.
Knowledge of mechanical testing methods for materials.
Knowledge of methods for selecting and using materials in mechanical engineering.

syllabus_topics: Defining and classifying material properties and testing methods
Defining structure, types of structures, atomic architecture, structural characterization methods
Structural states: crystalline structure, crystal lattices, crystallographic directions and planes, imperfections, non-crystalline solids
Alloy systems: phases and structural constituents, diffusion, solidification, phase equilibrium diagrams
Iron and Fe-C alloys - Fe-Fe3C, Fe-C equilibrium diagrams

Solid-state phase transformations in Fe-C alloys: thermodynamic conditions, transformations upon heating (pearlite to austenite transformation), transformations upon cooling (pearlitic, martensitic, bainitic transformation), tempering transformations
Preparation and examination of metallographic samples, macroscopic analysis, optical microscopy analysis and electron microscopy
Highlighting crystalline structure through X-ray diffraction
Mechanical testing methods – tensile, hardness, resilience tests
Quantitative determinations – non-metallic inclusion content, austenite grain size, proportion of phases and constituents
Construction and interpretation of equilibrium diagrams. Applications on the Fe-Fe3C diagram
Equilibrium structures of carbon steels, white cast irons and gray cast irons
Microstructures specific to isothermal and anisotropic transformation of supercooled austenite

assessment_methods.method: Practical activities evaluation (knowledge of theoretical concepts and understanding of experiments, discussions)

assessment_rules: A minimum average grade of 5 is required for laboratory work assessments. Basic knowledge of theoretical subjects and understanding of fundamental principles in practical applications are necessary to pass the course.
